page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Plasticity defined
steps.margin_note: Definition in four lines. Mention both triggers: environment and phase of life.
lines: PLASTICITY is the ability of a plant to follow
different pathways, in response to the
environment or to its phase of life, and so to
steps.why: The same plant with the same genes builds different structures in different conditions, which is what makes the ability worth naming.
common_mistakes: Saying plasticity is a genetic change. The genes do not change; only the structure does.
Leaving out 'in response to the environment'. The response is the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Same plant, same genes, different shape.

steps.label: Example
steps.margin_note: Name the term and at least two plants. The water example is a useful extra.

lines.text: Heterophylly: different leaves on one plant

lines: Example: HETEROPHYLLY in cotton and coriander.
The juvenile leaves of these plants are shaped
differently from the adult leaves on the same
In buttercup, leaves grown under water differ
steps.why: One plant carrying two leaf shapes at once is the clearest possible demonstration that the difference comes from conditions and not from genes.
common_mistakes: Naming heterophylly without a plant. Cotton and coriander are the named ones.
Calling it a difference between two plants. It is a difference within ONE plant.
steps.memory_tip: Two leaf shapes on one plant is plasticity you can see.
